title: Which cooking oil is the best?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: (something) encourage people to use or do (something)
informal phrase used to express frustration or surprise
an item, usually food or medicine, that people think is very effective or beneficial

sentences.en: Hello and welcome to 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听 BBC 英语教学的 6 分钟英语。

sentences.en: I'm Georgie. And I'm Neil. Georgie, today we're talking about cooking oils and which products are best for our health.
sentences.zh: 我是 Georgie。我是 Neil。Georgie，今天我们来聊聊食用油，以及哪种油对我们的健康最好。

sentences.en: What do you use to cook with? Olive oil?
sentences.zh: 你平时炒菜用什么？橄榄油？

sentences.en: Butter? Maybe avocado oil? Hmm, when I want my food to be rich and creamy, I use butter, but usually for everyday meals I just use olive oil.
sentences.zh: 黄油？也许是牛油果油？嗯，当我希望食物浓郁奶香时，我会用黄油，但平时做家常菜我一般只用橄榄油。

sentences.en: What about you? Yes, it varies, but I guess for East Asian food, I might sometimes use sesame oil.
sentences.zh: 你呢？对，这不固定，不过我想做东亚菜时，我有时会用香油。

sentences.en: Now, there are so many different oils we can use for our food, and some of them are very expensive and claim to have big health benefits.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们可以用来做饭的油种类繁多，其中一些非常昂贵，并声称有很大的健康益处。

sentences.en: Today we'll be finding out whether these products are worth the money and can really help us eat more healthily.
sentences.zh: 今天我们将探讨这些产品是否物有所值，是否真的能帮我们吃得更健康。

sentences.en: Yes, and don't forget to go to our website for a transcript of this programme to read along, and a worksheet to test what you've learned.
sentences.zh: 是的，别忘了访问我们的网站获取本期节目的文字稿以便对照阅读，还有一份练习题来测试你学到的内容。

sentences.en: Visit bbclearningenglish.com. OK. Georgie, let's start with a question.
sentences.zh: 请访问 bbclearningenglish.com。好的。Georgie，我们先从一个问题开始。

sentences.en: In the UK, a popular oil to cook with is olive oil, but which country produces the most olive oil?
sentences.zh: 在英国，做饭常用的一种油是橄榄油，但哪个国家生产的橄榄油最多？

sentences.en: Is it: a) Italy b) Greece c) Spain Ooh, that's difficult.
sentences.zh: 是：a) 意大利 b) 希腊 c) 西班牙 噢，这有点难。

sentences.en: I know that Spain produces a lot, but I think I'm going to go with Italy.
sentences.zh: 我知道西班牙产很多，但我猜我还是选意大利吧。

sentences.en: OK. Well, we'll find out if that's the right answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的。好吧，我们在节目结束时揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Now, lots of us are careful about the amount of fat we eat.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们很多人都对摄入的脂肪量很在意。

sentences.en: We might avoid fast food and treats like chocolate or cake, but lots of the fat we eat comes from the oils we use to cook with.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会避开快餐以及巧克力或蛋糕之类的零食，但我们吃掉的很多脂肪都来自于我们做饭用的油。

sentences.en: Yes, and some expensive oils claim to contain other vitamins that are good for us.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且一些昂贵的油声称含有对我们有益的其他维生素。

sentences.en: But are these claims true? It can be confusing.
sentences.zh: 但这些说法是真的吗？这可能会让人感到困惑。

sentences.en: Presenter of BBC Radio 4 programme Sliced Bread, Greg Foot, has lots of emails about the problem.
sentences.zh: BBC Radio 4 节目《Sliced Bread》的主持人 Greg Foot 收到了很多关于这个问题的电子邮件。

sentences.en: I'll tell you what, Sarah – we have had an absolute wok-load of emails sent to sliced.bread@bbc.co.uk asking about cooking oils.
sentences.zh: 跟你说实话，Sarah——我们收到了巨量的发往 sliced.bread@bbc.co.uk 的电子邮件，都在询问关于食用油的事情。

sentences.en: Listener Alastair in Midlothian wrote that: "For years we were told to cook with polyunsaturated oils like sunflower oil.
sentences.zh: 中洛锡安的听众 Alastair 写道：“多年来，人们告诉我们要用多不饱和油，比如葵花籽油。

sentences.en: But now all the YouTube doctor experts are telling us seed oils are harmful.
sentences.zh: 但现在所有的油管医生专家都在告诉我们，种子油是有害的。

sentences.en: They advocate consuming extra-virgin olive oil, but as I understand it that's not suitable for frying a fish.
sentences.zh: 他们提倡食用特级初榨橄榄油，但据我所知，那并不适合炸鱼。

sentences.en: Also, I hear that over a certain temperature olive oil turns harmful.
sentences.zh: 另外，我听说超过一定温度橄榄油就会变得有害。

sentences.en: What the heck do I use for frying and roasting?"
sentences.zh: 到底该用什么来煎和烤？”

sentences.en: Greg says that he has received a wok-load of emails.
sentences.zh: Greg 说他收到了大量的电子邮件。

sentences.en: A load of something is a lot of something.
sentences.zh: a load of something 的意思就是“大量某物”。

sentences.en: You'll also commonly hear the expressions shed-load or truck-load.
sentences.zh: 你通常也会听到 shed-load 或 truck-load 这样的表达。

sentences.en: These are used to emphasise how much of something there is.
sentences.zh: 这些词用来强调某事物的数量很多。

sentences.en: Yes, and Greg uses wok-load as a fun expression, because he's talking about cooking oils and a wok is a kind of pan.
sentences.zh: 是的，Greg 用 wok-load 作为一个有趣的表达，因为他在谈论食用油，而 wok（炒锅）是一种锅。

sentences.en: Greg reads one of the emails from a confused listener, Alastair, who says that he's watched YouTube videos that argue that oils like sunflower oil are bad for you.
sentences.zh: Greg 读了一位困惑的听众 Alastair 的来信，Alastair 说他看了一些油管视频，这些视频认为葵花籽油之类的油对健康有害。

sentences.en: These videos advocate using extra-virgin olive oil.
sentences.zh: 这些视频提倡使用特级初榨橄榄油。

sentences.en: If you advocate something, you encourage people to use it.
sentences.zh: 如果你 advocate 某事，你就是鼓励人们去使用它。

sentences.en: But Alastair has also heard bad things about olive oil, and that you can't use it at high temperatures.
sentences.zh: 但 Alastair 也听到了一些关于橄榄油的负面说法，说它不能用于高温烹饪。

sentences.en: He asks, what the heck can he use for roasting and frying?
sentences.zh: 他问，到底（what the heck）可以用什么来烤和煎？

sentences.en: What the heck is an informal phrase we can use to express frustration or surprise.
sentences.zh: what the heck 是一个非正式短语，用来表达挫折感或惊讶。

sentences.en: It does seem like there's a lot of advice about cooking oils and that not everyone agrees.
sentences.zh: 看起来关于食用油的建议确实很多，而且并非所有人都意见一致。

sentences.en: Yes, and some of the advice is to use very expensive options such as coconut oil and avocado oil.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且有些建议是使用非常昂贵的油，比如椰子油和牛油果油。

sentences.en: People who advocate using these oils say they are wonder products.
sentences.zh: 提倡使用这些油的人说它们是奇效产品（wonder product）。

sentences.en: A wonder product is an item, usually a food or medicine, that is very effective or beneficial for people.
sentences.zh: wonder product 是一种物品，通常是食物或药物，对人非常有效或有益。

sentences.en: But not everyone is convinced that expensive cooking oils are worth the money.
sentences.zh: 但并非所有人都相信昂贵的食用油物有所值。

sentences.en: Nita Forouhi is professor of population health and nutrition at the University of Cambridge and she talked to BBC Radio 4's Sliced Bread host, Greg Foot, about expensive cooking oils like avocado oil.
sentences.zh: Nita Forouhi 是剑桥大学的人口健康与营养学教授，她接受了 BBC Radio 4 《Sliced Bread》节目主持人 Greg Foot 的采访，谈论了像牛油果油这样昂贵的食用油。

sentences.en: What do you think, Nita? What might justify the price tag?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看，Nita？是什么证明了这个价格的合理性？

sentences.en: Certainly, avocado oil is good for all the reasons mentioned, but is it worth justifying the cost?
sentences.zh: 当然，牛油果油有提到的种种好处，但它值得这个成本吗？

sentences.en: If you're a particular connoisseur of the taste it brings, and you prefer it and you have the money, then knock yourself out.
sentences.zh: 如果你对它带来的风味情有独钟，并且你更喜欢它，手头又宽裕，那就尽管去买吧（knock yourself out）。

sentences.en: But there's lots of myths about these super foods and wonder oils and wonder this and that.
sentences.zh: 但关于这些超级食物、神奇油类以及各种奇效东西，有很多神话般的传言。

sentences.en: And it's just all, I'm afraid, hogwash. Nita says that avocado oil does have some health benefits, but she's not sure they are worth the cost of a bottle.
sentences.zh: 而这一切，恐怕都是一派胡言（hogwash）。Nita 表示牛油果油确实有一些健康益处，但她不确定这些益处是否对得起一瓶油的价格。

sentences.en: She says if you like the taste and are happy to spend the money then ' knock yourself out'.
sentences.zh: 她说如果你喜欢这个味道并且乐意花钱，那就“尽管买吧（knock yourself out）”。

sentences.en: The expression knock yourself out means go ahead.
sentences.zh: 表达 knock yourself out 的意思是“请便”或“自便”。

sentences.en: But Nita is also concerned about all the health claims about expensive wonder products like avocado oil.
sentences.zh: 但 Nita 也对所有关于昂贵奇效产品（如牛油果油）的健康宣称感到担忧。

sentences.en: She says that many claims are hogwash: they are nonsense, and products are not worth spending money on.
sentences.zh: 她说许多说法都是一派胡言（hogwash）：纯属无稽之谈，这些产品根本不值得花钱去买。

sentences.en: OK. Maybe I'll stick to my olive oil then.
sentences.zh: 好吧。那我可能还是坚持用我的橄榄油吧。

sentences.en: And that reminds me of your question, Neil.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起了你的问题，Neil。

sentences.en: Yes, I asked you which country produces the most olive oil.
sentences.zh: 是的，我问你哪个国家生产的橄榄油最多。

sentences.en: And I said Italy. And I'm afraid you are wrong.
sentences.zh: 而我说的是意大利。恐怕你猜错了。

sentences.en: No! It is in fact Spain. OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned in this programme, starting with a load of something, which means a lot of something.
sentences.zh: 不会吧！事实上是西班牙。好吧。让我们回顾一下本期节目中学到的词汇，首先是 a load of something，意思是大量某物。

sentences.en: We also commonly hear shed-load and truck-load.
sentences.zh: 我们也很常听到 shed-load 和 truck-load。

sentences.en: If you advocate something, you encourage people to use it or do it.
sentences.zh: 如果你 advocate 某事，你就是鼓励人们使用它或做它。

sentences.en: The expression what the heck is used to express frustration or surprise.
sentences.zh: 表达 what the heck 用于表达挫折感或惊讶。

sentences.en: A wonder product is something that people think is very effective or beneficial.
sentences.zh: wonder product 是指人们认为非常有效或有益的东西。

sentences.en: The expression knock yourself out means go ahead.
sentences.zh: 表达 knock yourself out 的意思是“请便”。

sentences.en: And if something is described as hogwash, it's nonsense or not true.
sentences.zh: 如果某事被描述为 hogwash，那就是胡说八道或并非事实。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. Try the free interactive quiz on our website to test the vocabulary you've learned.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了。快去试试我们网站上的免费互动小测验，测试一下你学到的词汇吧。

sentences.en: Visit bbclearningenglish.com. Goodbye for now!
sentences.zh: 请访问 bbclearningenglish.com。下次见！

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
